description: Retrieval baseline and live-review cases for the model-selected grid (get_grid): two lists of library things and the fact where each pair meets. Each case gives the visitor's question, a get_grid (or, for the negative case, aggregate_data) call a good answer would make, the pinned facts that call returns, and the failures to watch for when reading the live page. The arguments are one reasonable call, not the only one: the model chooses its own rows, columns and span, so a live run is judged on the page, not on matching these arguments. Pinned facts were measured 2026-10-10 against the deploy-built SQLite store; the Spring '77 Scarlet > Fire lengths were re-measured 2026-10-11 after the release-track pass linked more Dick's Picks and Road Trips tracks to their performances. The Dick's Picks and guest cases were measured 2026-10-11 against the same store after the data pass that completed the 36 Dick's Picks volumes and folded duplicate guests onto one person id. They move whenever a data pass adds shows, setlists or release tracks; regenerate them against the live store rather than trusting this file blindly. Live results are in docs/measurements/2026-10-10-grids.md and docs/measurements/2026-10-11-grids-task9.md.

cases.question: Compare Dark Star and Playing in the Band over time.
cases.page_expectation: A grid of the two songs across the years, or a chart per song (this question also lives in data-charts-v1); either shows the hand-off from Dark Star's late-sixties peak to Playing in the Band's long steady run.
failure_conditions: The page answers with a wall of yearly numbers in prose instead of a grid or chart the visitor can scan.
A yearly count in the words disagrees with the grid or chart beside it.
Presents 1967-1968 Dark Star counts as the whole story without saying how few of those years' shows have a surviving setlist.
Shows only one of the two songs while presenting it as the comparison.

cases.question: Tell me about the Europe '72 tour.
cases.page_expectation: The tour's 22 nights as rows against a few songs that tell the tour's story (the big jams, a signature song), with the most telling nights open and a few cells pointed at, so the visitor can see the run and hear any night.
failure_conditions: No grid and no other way to see the tour's nights side by side or to hear them.
A night or song length named in the words that is not in the grid's cells.
Columns that say nothing about the tour (songs played once, or every song at equal weight) when the result suggested the songs played most.

cases.question: Which nights of Spring '77 had Scarlet > Fire, and how long?
cases.page_expectation: The tour's nights that had the pairing, with each half's length from the library and the longest pairings pointed at.
failure_conditions: A length in the words or a highlight note that is not the grid's cell (lengths invented or remembered by the model).
Fills in a length for April 25 at Passaic, where the library has the pairing but no length.
Lists nights that had Scarlet Begonias without Fire on the Mountain as Scarlet > Fire nights, or misses that April 29 had Scarlet alone.
Answers with a prose list of dates and minutes the visitor cannot scan or play.

cases.question: How did The Other One and Dark Star trade places on Europe '72?
cases.page_expectation: The 22 nights against the two songs, so the alternation is visible at a glance, with Bickershaw (May 7) pointed at as the one night that had both.
failure_conditions: Misses the Bickershaw exception: May 7, 1972 had both songs (Dark Star 20 minutes, The Other One 31).
Claims a strict alternation the grid's cells contradict.
No grid, so the visitor must read 22 dates in prose to see the pattern.

cases.question: Which Dick's Picks should I start with?
cases.page_expectation: A few volumes recommended by what is on them and why, with a way to see the series side by side (a grid of records against the songs that tell them apart, album cards, or a ranked pick list) and to hear the records named. The volumes picked lead; the rest can wait behind Show all.
failure_conditions: Recommends volumes without saying what is on them that makes each a good place to start.
A song length or track count in the words that the library's tracklists do not show (Dark Star on Dick's Picks 36 runs 37 minutes on one track).
Claims a volume lacks a song when a track on it names no song but mentions it, such as Scarlet Begonias inside Nassau '81's medley track.
Names a volume or its date and venue wrongly, or recommends a Dick's Picks volume the library does not have.
Gives the visitor no way to hear or open the records it recommends.

cases.question: Who sat in with the Dead?
cases.page_expectation: The guests who sat in most, with how often and when, so the visitor sees who belonged to which era (a grid of guests across the years, a ranked list of guests, or guest appearance cards), and a few nights worth hearing.
failure_conditions: A guest's count of shows in the words that differs from the library's guest credits (Ned Lagin 33, Bruce Hornsby 16 as a guest).
Lists the same person twice under two names.
Calls a band member a guest, or a guest a member, without saying which years each applies to.
Answers with a list of names and no sense of when each sat in or how often.

cases.question: Which songs did they play most in 1977, and when in the year?
cases.page_expectation: A ranking (ranked_list or data_chart by song) answers which songs; when in the year is a tour or month question that a chart, the tours, or a few show cards answer. A song x year grid of one year is the wrong shape and would mean the grid had become a keyword route.
failure_conditions: Draws a song x year grid with a single 1977 column, which says nothing a ranking does not.
States a count in the words that differs from the ranking's rows.
Counts Drums as a song without the title or a note saying so.
